topic_summary: Requiring short video demos attached to pull requests eliminates live review meetings and saves founder focus.
Replacing lengthy take-home coding projects with a realistic PR debugging task evaluates a developer candidate's real-world skills much faster.
Adding a single-click staging data reset prevents ghost bugs caused by messy client testing during QA.
Requiring developers to explain AI-generated code during PR reviews maintains code quality without slowing down boilerplate generation.
Adding automated error monitoring to launch checklists lets small agencies catch post-launch bugs before clients notice.
Replacing manual setup documentation with an automated executable script reduces setup friction and saves developer hours during project context-switching.
Enforcing a strict 30-minute limit on debugging alone prevents developers from wasting billable hours in quiet isolation.
Requiring developers to document the reasoning behind code choices in PRs prevents wasted dev hours when maintaining client projects later.
Wrapping third-party frontend widgets in isolated error boundaries prevents external API outages from breaking client web applications.
Requiring developers to write a failing test before fixing a client bug prevents recurring regressions and saves agency reputation.
Opening draft pull requests within hours of starting a task gives tech leads early visibility to catch bad architectural choices before dev time is wasted.
Wrapping incomplete client features in simple feature flags keeps the main branch continuously deployable and eliminates emergency release delays.
Requiring developers to convert informal Slack requests into structured, time-capped tickets before coding prevents unbilled scope creep.
Requiring developers to test UI features under simulated slow network conditions catches unhandled loading states before client demos.
Enforcing local API mocking before UI integration prevents frontend development delays caused by external client API dependencies.
Requiring a brief rollback plan in pull requests with database or API changes prevents botched deployments and emergency client calls.
Shipping a minor fix to production on a new developer's first day validates pipeline access and onboarding efficiency.
Replacing live coding interviews with an async PR review task evaluates real-world developer skills while saving founder interview time.
Automated pull request preview deployments prevent clients from testing incomplete work and filing false bug reports on staging.
Replacing live daily standups with end-of-day async Slack updates protects developer focus and gives founders a clear progress trail.
Standardizing on a single default tech stack across client projects prevents technical sprawl and speeds up cross-project maintenance.
Restricting opportunistic refactoring strictly to files touched in the active ticket prevents bloated PRs and unexpected client regressions.
Requiring developers to include a 3-step testing guide in pull requests lets non-technical agency staff quickly verify client features without back-and-forth questions.
Restricting dependency updates to dedicated monthly maintenance windows prevents mid-sprint production bugs in client projects.
Requiring developers to present two solutions and a recommendation when reporting technical blockers saves founder decision-making time.
Time-boxing technical spikes on third-party integrations before quoting project timelines prevents costly agency scope creep.
Automated CI checks for updated `.env.example` files prevent developer onboarding and context-switching delays across client projects.
Requiring developers to explain AI-generated code in PR reviews prevents unvetted logic and edge-case bugs from entering client codebases.
Wrapping risky client features in feature flags allows teams to instantly disable buggy updates without emergency code deployments.
Requiring standardized local database seeders with edge-case data prevents UI layout breaks and visual bugs before client demos.
